recent_posts.title: Leveraging The Super Keyword In Custom Elements
recent_posts.summary: The `super` keyword in custom elements extends beyond just calling it first in constructors. You don't need to invoke the constructor at all unless adding to it. The `super` keyword can be used outside constructors to call parent methods like `connectedCallback()`, and `super.observedAttributes` with spread syntax avoids redeclaring inherited attributes. This approach leverages inheritance to reduce code duplication and simplify maintenance of custom element libraries.

recent_posts.title: How To Dynamically Install Custom Elements
recent_posts.summary: A reusable pattern for dynamically loading custom elements without bundling. The approach uses naming conventions (class names matching file names with a configurable suffix), static initialization blocks for self-registration, and dynamic imports to load only the custom elements present in the DOM. The pattern supports both initial page load and runtime element insertion via MutationObserver, includes interdependency handling through custom events, and achieves tree-shaking benefits without requiring a build step. Complete implementation is approximately 1KB.

recent_posts.title: Accessible Rickrolling
recent_posts.summary: The parity principle in web accessibility emphasizes that all users should have comparable experiences, not necessarily better ones. Using rickrolling as an example, the author demonstrates how well-intentioned accessibility fixes can actually reduce accessibility by breaking parity between different user groups. The piece distinguishes between accessibility (gaining access) and inclusion (not wishing you hadn't), arguing that good writing skills are essential for accessible interfaces and cannot be automated or tested programmatically.

recent_posts.title: Hel: A 3-Axis, Obliterated Variable Font
recent_posts.summary: Hel is a deliberately distorted variable font with three customizable axes: Slant for faux italics, Warp for character distortion effects, and Shrink for baseline disruption. The font includes 80 glyphs, 15 contextual alternates, and is designed for creating gritty, DIY aesthetic web pages while maintaining performance through CSS font-variation-settings animation rather than resource-intensive SVG filters.

recent_posts.title: Skune: A hand drawn variable font
recent_posts.summary: Skune is a new variable font featuring hand-drawn glyphs with a punk aesthetic. The font includes a Slant axis that rotates glyphs rather than distorting them, and comes in two variants: the standard Skune and Skune Punch (a stencil-like version with filled counters). Each font contains 62 glyphs including uppercase letters, numbers, punctuation, and symbols, with files approximately 30KB each.

recent_posts.title: Advertising? On my blog?
recent_posts.summary: A web developer and writer explains their decision to add advertising to their blog after struggling with traditional monetization methods. They describe implementing ethical, non-tracking ads that promote only their own creative work - books, fonts, accessibility resources, and merchandise. The ads are designed to be accessible, clearly marked, and free of JavaScript tracking, representing a compromise between financial necessity and maintaining user experience principles.

recent_posts.title: The col element
recent_posts.summary: The HTML col element, used with colgroup, allows grouping table columns but creates complex, poorly supported structures. The element's behavior is counterintuitive - it doesn't contain columns but sets a schema for groupings, and CSS classes applied to col elements mysteriously affect other table cells. Screen reader support for spanned and grouped columns is unreliable across different assistive technologies. Simple table headers without complex grouping provide better accessibility and user comprehension than elaborate column structures.

recent_posts.title: The caption element
recent_posts.summary: The HTML <caption> element is used for labeling tables and plays a crucial role in web accessibility. Unlike the <summary> attribute which provides non-visible descriptions, the <caption> element is directly associated with tables, improving the experience for screen reader users. The CSS property caption-side can adjust the positioning of captions, but may affect accessibility if visual and source orders conflict. Best practices suggest using headings with captions to enhance user experience, particularly for screen reader users.

recent_posts.title: The code element
recent_posts.summary: This post dives into the intricacies of using markdown to produce HTML markup, focusing on the meta aspects of markup languages and markdown's role in generating them. It explains how backticks and escape characters are used to display code elements properly and offers readers a humorous exploration of self-referential language concepts.

recent_posts.title: The cite element
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the HTML cite element's intended use for citing the title of a work. It highlights changes between HTML4 and HTML5, explaining that the element should not be used for person names or non-title references. The article encourages users not to stress about the use of <cite>, while critiquing the naming convention of the element.
